article_content: Older people with memory problems may boost their brainpower with fish oil supplements, researchers say. Healthy individuals with mild memory deficits, particularly in recalling past events, showed improved memory after six months of treatment. An overview of evidence suggests that the omega-3 fatty acid DHA has the most benefit for people with existing memory issues, especially when coping with physical or mental stress. Experts believe DHA-rich supplements from fish oils or other marine sources might slow or prevent mental decline, as DHA is found in reduced amounts in people with Alzheimer's disease. DHA is thought to help nerve cells communicate with each other. The richest source of DHA is oily fish like herring, mackerel, and sardines. Britons are advised to eat at least one portion of oily fish a week, but only one in three do so. A review by US and Canadian scientists found several studies examining the effect of DHA supplements on memory. The MIDAS study, involving 485 healthy elderly people with memory complaints, found that 24 weeks of marine oil supplements led to 'significant improvements' in memory test scores. Benefits of DHA are most observed in ageing individuals with mild cognitive impairment or memory complaints, or those under chronic stress. Dr. Carrie Ruxton, an independent public health nutritionist, noted falling oily fish consumption among Britons, with average intake at 90g weekly compared to the recommended 140g. She stated that 'studies have shown fish oils lead to better performance in working and verbal memory, indicating the potential to delay cognitive decline.'

article_content: People living in UK cities may be familiar with colourful murals appearing overnight, but this could be the world's most geeky graffiti. The wall art, created in London, Birmingham, and Bristol, challenges the public to break codes for a chance to win tickets to a technology fair. The artwork includes code alongside notable technological minds, such as Alan Turing. To the untrained eye, the wall art may display nonsensical numbers and patterns, but it actually contains code, including Morse code, JavaScript, and Binary code, that hides a secret message. The graffiti is part of a bid to interest young people in coding, essential for developing computer software. Alan Turing, considered the 'godfather of computer science', is featured in two murals, as this month marks the 75th anniversary of the Government Code and Cypher Schools' arrival at Bletchley Park. Turing and his team broke the Enigma machine code used by the Nazis, a significant turning point in World War Two. The graffiti also features contemporary coding heroes, such as Nolan Bushnell, who created Atari, and Jon 'Maddog' Hall, executive director of Linux. The artwork was commissioned by Campus Party, a technology festival and coding school, to be held at the O2 in London from 2 to 7 September.

On this news, Li-Cycle shares declined by $1.04, or 'nearly half', to close at $1.23 per share on October 23, 2023, on 'unusually heavy' trading volume. Security and defense policy | Uncategorized Lithuania continues the steady supply of assistance to Ukraine with a new shipment of advanced 200 kW power generators, field beds and rations delivered today. Stationary 200 kW diesel-run power generators solve power issues in areas without or with damaged electricity provision. The equipment come with devices that switch on and off the generator's engine depending on the presence and absence of power supply from stationary infrastructure. The assistance was taken to Ukraine by the Lithuanian Armed Forces. Besides the military vehicles and equipment, Lithuania also provides active training assistance to the Ukrainian military, takes in injured servicemembers for medical care, arranges expert consultations and contributes financially to international funds of assistance to Ukraine. Lithuania has also approved a long-term assistance plan for Ukraine: a new EUR 300 million-worth package is planned for 2024-2026. In total, the assistance provided so far is worth over EUR 1.5 billion, or more than 1.4 percent of GDP, and half of it is military assistance.

article_content: State Secretary Bjørg Sandkjær is representing Norway at the humanitarian conference in support of the people of Gaza on November 9 in Paris. 'I am appalled by the alleged scale of human and material destruction in Gaza. More than 15,000 people have reportedly been killed, with sources suggesting the number could be 'much higher'. Hamas must release the hostages they have taken immediately,' said State Secretary Bjørg Sandkjær. The conference is attended by representatives from several key countries, the UN and other organisations that contribute to the humanitarian efforts in Gaza. The Palestinian Authorities (PA) are represented by Prime Minister Mohammad Shtayyeh. One month after the war started, the situation in Gaza is 'catastrophic and rapidly deteriorating'. Of the 15,000 people killed, more than 6,000 are children. For a month, the inhabitants have lived in constant fear. They lack essential goods such as water, food and medicine. It will take many years and billions of dollars to rebuild Gaza. 'All parties to this war are obliged to follow humanitarian law. This means that they must protect civilians and that attacks must distinguish between military targets and civilians, and civilian infrastructure. The parties are also obliged to ensure that vital emergency aid arrives people in need, even if fighting is ongoing. We are very concerned that even more civilians will be killed as Israel intensifies the ground war in Gaza City,' said Sandkjær. Sandkjær also calls for more support for the Palestinians: 'Norway has increased the humanitarian assistance to the Palestinians by NOK 300 million since the crisis began. We urge other countries to increase the humanitarian assistance and to continue to support the Palestinian Authority. The PA is crucial for the Palestinian population not only in the West Bank, but also in Gaza. If the authorities in the West Bank collapse, Israel will not have a negotiating partner when it is possible to resume peace negotiations,' said State Secretary Sandkjær.
